extraction.Name: Minnie Lessert
extraction.Refused/Protested: she was forced to accept the patent in fee received by her
extraction.Recorded patent: This instrument was recorded soon after same was received, the exact being unknown, by R. C. Lessert and Clair C. Long
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: the land in question was sold, the proceeds being used for the purchase of cattle, date of sale unknown
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: the land was not sold to pay debts or taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: she is working every day for a living; employed by the United States Government
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, in good health; assists her husband in the support of their four minor children; received $900.00 from the sale of this land, which amount she figures was not a fair price; states she was not defrauded of her property; has not received any aid from the Government, state or County since her patent in fee was issued; document received at Pine Ridge Agency May 11, 1929 | Source review 2026-04-27: Minnie Lessert is a Pine Ridge (Oglala Sioux) allottee who had relocated to Leupp, Arizona by the time of the affidavit. Affidavit sworn before notary in Coconino County, Arizona, on May 4, 1929; received at Pine Ridge Agency May 11, 1929 (visible Pine Ridge Agency receipt stamp on source). One-week mail interval between Coconino County execution and Pine Ridge Agency receipt. Notary commission expires 7/27/30. R.C. Lessert (named as her cousin in Joseph Lessert's parallel affidavit, allot 963) attended to recording the patent. Minnie figured the $900 sale price was not a fair price (her cousin Joseph's parallel affidavit said $900 was fair for his sale — same family, same transaction structure, different framings of fairness). BLM patent accession: 625271. Tribe/Reservation field corrected from 'Leupp Agency (Arizona)' which incorrectly conflated current residence with tribal affiliation. Pine Ridge agent demonstrably tracked relocated allottees to Arizona for testimony — administrative diligence worth noting in contrast to the Shawnee Agency's mailed-form-only approach (per Leech 1929).
